newsitem.title: SPAIN: TENNIS-COSTA IN TOP 10 AS SPANIARDS DOMINATE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COSTA IN TOP 10 AS SPANIARDS DOMINATE.

text.p: Albert Costa earned a place in the world's top 10 for the first time and a semifinal against close friend Carlos Moya in the Barcelona Open with a convincing quarter-final win over Cedric Pioline on Friday.

It was an excellent day for the local fans who were guaranteed a Spanish winner after former French Open finalist Alberto Berasategui and unknown qualifier Albert Portas also won their way through to the other semifinal.
Costa scored a comprehensive 6-4 6-2 win over Frenchman Pioline, while Moya beat Ukraine's Andrei Medvedev by the same score.
"Both on and off the court it will be tough...facing up to somebody who you spend most time with, here in Barcelona," said Moya.

Costa coped better with the difficult conditions after a stoppage for rain at 5-3 in the first set. Pioline's resistance crumbled after he squandered two points to break back to 5-5 after the restart.

"It was a complicated moment but he seemed to fall after that...and the second set was easier," said Costa, who said his opponent appeared tired after beating number one seed and holder Thomas Muster the previous day.
Moya had nearly let a 5-2 lead slip after a strong start in his match with Medvedev. But the Australian Open finalist shored up the errors in his game and ran out an easy winner.
Costa could yet overhaul Moya in the rankings if he wins the tournament and scores bonus points by beating world number 19 Berasategui.
Berasategui beat Brazil's Fernando Meligeni 6-2 7-5 and is clear favourite to prevail over Portas in the other semifinal.
Portas outwitted Morocco's Karim Alami with a series of wrong-footing double-fisted backhands and powerful forehand drives. He also won 6-2 7-5.
